about: Microsoft Entra diagnostic-settings log categories and the Log Analytics tables they land in (CLAUDE.md 5hf, 22 Nov 2026). Checked on Microsoft Learn 22 Nov 2026: learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/monitoring-health/concept-diagnostic-settings-logs-options and learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/reference/tables-category. MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs (preview, first-party service-to-service) is left out: Microsoft says it is not needed for investigations and its table name was not confirmed. AzureActivity is not an Entra category: it comes from the Azure subscription's activity log diagnostic setting.

tables.holds: changes to users, groups, apps, roles, policies, domains, Connect/sync and service settings
tables.useFor: any change an incident could make or that its attacker would need
phishing, AiTM, password spray, new country or device

tables.holds: sign-ins by a client on behalf of a user with a token or code
tables.useFor: token theft and replay, refresh-token abuse, device-code follow-up: usually only visible here
tables.note: Microsoft Learn (table reference, checked 22-23 Nov 2026) DESCRIBES Location here as 'The region of the resource emitting the event', while in SigninLogs Location is 'The 2 letter country code from where the sign-in occurred'. Not checked against tenant data. LocationDetails holds the sign-in location in both tables (a string here, dynamic in SigninLogs), so when you union the two take the country from parse_json(tostring(LocationDetails)).countryOrRegion - correct whichever way Location is filled.

tables.holds: app / service principal sign-ins with a secret or certificate
tables.useFor: stolen app secrets, malicious or over-privileged multi-tenant apps, vendor app abuse

tables.holds: provisioning to and from HR systems and SaaS apps
tables.useFor: rogue or changed provisioning, cross-tenant sync

tables.holds: AD FS sign-ins (Connect Health for AD FS)
tables.useFor: federation abuse, extranet lockout, risky IPs

tables.holds: users ID Protection rates as risky
tables.useFor: who is at risk after a campaign

tables.holds: ID Protection risk detections for users
tables.useFor: leaked credentials, anomalous token, unfamiliar sign-in properties

tables.holds: every HTTP request to Microsoft Graph in the tenant
tables.useFor: what a stolen token or app actually read or changed (mail, files, directory enumeration)

tables.holds: Global Secure Access traffic (Internet / Private Access)
tables.useFor: C2 or exfiltration destinations, blocked threat-intel hits

tables.holds: Microsoft 365 activity enriched by Global Secure Access
tables.useFor: M365 actions tied to network context

tables.holds: health of Global Secure Access remote networks
Azure Resource Manager operations on resources and resource providers
tables.useFor: changes made through an Azure resource provider of the affected service, e.g. Microsoft.ADHybridHealthService
